h1: Guard Retention: The Foundation of BJJ Defense
seo_title: BJJ Guard Retention: Concepts & Principles | BJJ Wiki
og_title: BJJ Guard Retention: Concepts & Principles | BJJ Wiki
description: Master the core concepts of guard retention in BJJ. Learn principles like frames, hip movement, and recovery to prevent guard passes.
intro_paragraphs: Guard retention is the practice of preventing your opponent from passing your guard.
Strong guard retention is the difference between a stuck white belt and a fluid blue belt.
It builds on principles of frames, hip movement, and active legs.

sections.heading: Why Guard Retention Matters
items: If you can't keep your guard, every roll devolves into a defensive scramble from side control or mount.
Guard retention extends your offensive opportunities by keeping you in a position where you can attack.

items.text: Always establish frames (forearm/knee shield) before trying to move.
Constant hip movement prevents your opponent from stabilizing their pass.
Your legs should always be doing something — hooking, pushing, or threatening.
Stop flattening out — get on your side and frame.
Don't wait for the pass; threaten attacks to force the opponent to defend.

faq.question: How long does it take to develop strong guard retention?
faq.answer: Most students see major improvement in 6-12 months of consistent training with deliberate focus.

faq.question: Should I work on retention or attacks first?
faq.answer: Both, but retention should never be neglected — without it, attacks have a short shelf life.
